source_text: De istorum enim peccatorum genere, quae multa esse et dimitti omnia per gratiam commendavit, ostendit se etiam illud unum superius dixisse peccatum; tu autem haec multa ea consentis esse, quae committuntur ab unoquoque homine motu propriae voluntatis; et illud ergo unum de eodem genere est.
pass_a_gloss: For from the kind of those sins, which he commended as many and all dismissed through grace, he showed that he had also said that one sin above; but you consent that these many are those which are committed by each human being by a motion of proper will; and that one therefore is of the same kind.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'

pass_b_english: For by commending these sins as many, and all forgiven through grace, he showed that the one sin he mentioned earlier also belonged to their kind. You agree that these many sins are those each human being commits by the movement of his own will. Therefore that one sin too belongs to the same kind.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
